newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Gains to Slovnaft shares boost Slovak bourse.
newsitem.headline: Gains to Slovnaft shares boost Slovak bourse.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) closed up in thinner trading on Tuesday as several major issues gained ground.
Lead by oil refiner Slovnaft, which was the largest advancer closing up 89 crowns at 779, the 12-share SAX index ended 6.34 points higher at 183.71.
Brokers remained guardedly optimistic saying the market was still fragile, lacking foreign investors as the country's political uncertainty overshadows its positive macroeconomic development.
Traders said they considered Slovnaft to be undervalued and has the potential to rise further.
"There is quite a large demand for Slovnaft at the moment, even at higher levels than today's close, so there seems to be enough room for it to rise further," said Radovan Dzugas of Creditanstalt.
Steel producer VSZ led floor trading with 9,700 shares changing hands, closing up 20 crowns at 660.
Brokers said VSZ's price appeared to reflect its current market value, though they added stronger demand at lower levels -- 650 crowns -- was expected to pull the stock's price lower.
Overall volume rose to 575,562 shares, boosted mainly by direct trades, from 116,600 traded on Monday. The turnover increased to 425.23 million crowns, from 98.85 million.
